# Dove of Hospice (`dove-of-hospice`)

Checks hospice billing deadlines and the cap: notices of election and of termination or revocation missing or late (with the days not covered), face-to-face encounters missing before the third and later benefit periods, the aggregate cap for the cap year, and a high live-discharge rate. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Dove never files notices of election or termination. Dove never submits or changes claims.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y dove-of-hospice demo
npx -y dove-of-hospice mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up hospice, made-up patients. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`census.csv`](fixtures/census.csv). Planted:
  - H1: elected November 2, NOE filed November 10 (due November 7), so 8 days are not covered.
  - H2: elected November 6 with no NOE on file (due November 11).
  - H3: revoked November 3 with no NOTR (due November 8).
  - H4: benefit period 4 started September 7 with no face-to-face encounter in the 30 days before.
  - H5: transferred in at period 3; period 4 starts December 24, so a face-to-face is coming due.
  - Cap year October 2025 to September 2026: five new elections (H3, H4, H6, H7, H8) and 205,000 paid against an estimated 176,807.20 cap.
  - Live discharges: 2 of the 4 discharges in the last 12 months (H3, H8) were live.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): an example cap amount of 35,361.44 per beneficiary (check the CMS figure for your cap year), cap year 2026, routine home care at 220 a day for the late-notice dollars, and a 20% live-discharge flag. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `dove_check` | List missing or late NOEs and NOTRs, missing or coming face-to-face encounters, the cap position and the live-discharge rate. | runs |
| `dove_write_report` | Write dove-hospice.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and dove-hospice.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/dove). | runs |
| `dove_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `dove_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `dove_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `dove_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `noe_submit` | Dove never files notices of election or termination. | refused |
| `claim_submit` | Dove never submits or changes claims. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `dove_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `patients` (required) | Hospice census under --root: patient, election date, NOE filed, discharge date and reason, NOTR filed, starting benefit period, face-to-face dates, Medicare paid in the cap year, cap share |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: cap_amount, cap_year, cap_warn_pct, daily_rate, noe_days, notr_days, f2f_window, warn_days, live_discharge_pct |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx dove-of-hospice inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Hospice patients (`patients`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `election` (required) | date | Election Date, Election, Admission Date, Admit Date, Admitted, Start of Care, SOC |
| `noe_filed` | date | NOE Filed, NOE Date, NOE Accepted, NOE Submitted, Notice of Election Filed |
| `discharge` | date | Discharge Date, Discharge, Discharged, Revocation Date, End Date, Date of Death |
| `discharge_reason` | text | Discharge Reason, Reason, Discharge Type, Disposition |
| `notr_filed` | date | NOTR Filed, NOTR Date, NOTR Submitted, Notice of Termination Filed |
| `starting_period` | number | Starting Period, Benefit Period, First Period, Period at Admission |
| `f2f` | text | F2F Dates, F2F, Face to Face, Face-to-Face Dates, F2F Encounter |
| `cap_paid` | amount | Cap Year Paid, Medicare Paid, Paid, Payments |
| `cap_share` | number | Cap Share, Beneficiary Share, Proportional Share, Beneficiary Count |

## Settings file (`dove_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cap_amount` | Per-beneficiary cap amount for the cap year (CMS publishes it each year); no cap check without it |
| `cap_year` | Cap year to check, named by the year it ends (2026 = October 1 2025 to September 30 2026); default the one holding as_of |
| `cap_warn_pct` | Percent of the cap at which to warn; default 90 |
| `daily_rate` | Routine home care daily rate, for dollars on late notices; default 0 |
| `noe_days` | Calendar days to file the NOE; default 5 |
| `notr_days` | Calendar days to file the NOTR; default 5 |
| `f2f_window` | Days before a period starts that a face-to-face may happen; default 30 |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to list face-to-face encounters coming due; default 45 |
| `live_discharge_pct` | Live discharge rate over 12 months to flag; default 20 |

## Memory

`dove_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `dove_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dove-of-hospice": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "dove-of-hospice",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add dove-of-hospice -- npx -y dove-of-hospice mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
dove-of-hospice tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
dove-of-hospice sources               # the columns each input is read from
dove-of-hospice inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
dove-of-hospice call dove_check '{"patients":"<patients>"}'
dove-of-hospice eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
dove-of-hospice demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
